title: Veronese numerator compatibility with tensor-power transitions
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], L an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], d,n,b natural numbers, and s a degree-d element of the section ring of L [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. For a section t of O_X tensor (L tensorPow d) tensorPow n, define a_n(t) as the underlying section-ring element of sectionRingVeroneseNumerator [def-sc-section-ring-veronese-fraction-map]. Then a_(n+b)(mulTensorPowSection(homOfGlobalSection(L tensorPow d,s_d),O_X,n,b)(t))=a_n(t)*s^b, with the transition from [def-sc-section-fraction-presentation]. No nonvanishing, reducedness, or regularity hypothesis is required.

source.place: Equation module-invert-s (Tag 0B5L), Lemma 01PW(2), and the Veronese localization in the proof of Lemma 01Q1

proof.text: Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSectionRing and reuse its proved private tensorPowAddIso_assoc_inv and eqToHom_app_heq rather than duplicating their statements. Induct on n to prove tensorPowMulIso_add_inv: the zero case is left-unitor naturality; the successor uses associator naturality, the induction hypothesis and the imported associativity theorem, reassociated with reassoc_of%. Thus regrouping d-fold blocks commutes with concatenation.

Prove the transition for exponent one. Expand the numerator as its direct-sum injection after tensorPowMulIso inverse and the left unitor. The left unitor takes mulTensorPowSection to concatenation with tensorPowSectionOne. The exponent-one tensor section transported back by tensorPowMulIso is the original section: expand tensorPowMulIso at one, use tensorPowAddIso_zero_inv from InvertibleSectionRing, and apply the right unitor. DirectSum.of_mul_of and tensorPowMulIso_add_inv then identify the one-step numerator with multiplication by s. No ring_power_of theorem or general homogeneous power calculation is needed.

Induct on b. Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FractionZeroTensorPower and reuse its proved private mulTensorPowSection_zero and mulTensorPowSection_comp. At b=0 the transition is the identity and the ring power is one. At b+1, composition with the one-step transition, the inductive numerator identity, pow_succ and ring associativity give the claimed formula. The associativity exponent transport in the composition theorem is definitionally the identity for its final exponent one. This works for d=0, n=0, b=0, and zero s. No hypotheses, definition, or unit route change.

lean.statement:
theorem sectionRingVeroneseNumerator_transition
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (d : ℕ) (s : sectionRingGrade L d) (n b : ℕ)
    (t : Γ((𝟙_ X.Modules) ⊗ (L.tensorPow d).tensorPow n, ⊤)) :
    (sectionRingVeroneseNumerator X L d (n + b)
      ((mulTensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection (L.tensorPow d) (s.val d))
        (𝟙_ X.Modules) n b).app ⊤ t)).val =
      (sectionRingVeroneseNumerator X L d n t).val * s.val ^ b
